descriptionChirho: An open public space in a Greco-Roman town serving as the commercial and social center where goods were bought and sold, people gathered, children played (Matthew 11:16, Luke 7:32), and religious leaders sought greetings and prominence (Matthew 23:7, Mark 12:38, Luke 11:43, 20:46); also where idle laborers waited for hire (Matthew 20:3) and Paul debated daily (Acts 17:17). Spanish uses both plaza and mercado, Arabic renders it الأَسْواقِ/سوقِ (suq, 'market'), Korean uses 장터/시장 (market), Hindi बाज़ार (bazar), Swahili soko/masoko. The two clusters differ only in grammatical number: plural dative (S61191) versus singular forms (S61192), with no semantic distinction.
